Hi Sarah — great demo today, thanks for the constructive questions.  Below is a concise post-demo summary focused on SLOs, acceptance criteria, and the proposed plan-of-action (MOP) so we can align on decision criteria and next steps.  Please confirm or flag changes.

Key SLO candidates (proposed):
- Latency (single-turn text generation): 95th percentile <= 300 ms (token stream to client start <= 150 ms)
- End-to-end response completion: median <= 180 ms, 99th <= 500 ms (depends on client-side processing)
- Sustained throughput: 200 QPS across the cluster with P95 latency target maintained
- Concurrency target: support 32 concurrent active sessions per customer instance without SLO degradation
- Streaming: first partial token delivered to the client within 120–150 ms of request start; incremental tokens streamed continuously thereafter

Assumptions/constraints:
- Workload: short-turn assistant queries (20–80 tokens generated), occasional long completions up to 512 tokens for summarization
- Model family: mid-sized open models we discussed — will test both float16 and int8 quantized variants
- Deployment mode: initial pilot on Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to get predictable latency; optionally fall back to hosted with routing policies for scale

Proposed acceptance checklist (attached: SLO_checklist_v1.pdf):
1) Baseline perf run showing P95 <= target under synthetic mixed-tenancy load
2) Streaming handshake validated on Android and web clients with real packet timing
3) Throughput sustained at target for 30-minute window without token error spikes
4) Failover behavior validated (regional fallback)

Immediate next steps / MAP items:
- Redwood: schedule benchmark run window and provide perf test plan + test harness (we attach perf_test_plan.xlsx).
- Bluehaven: provide a small representative test corpus + a contact from infra/engineering (would love to include Mike in the test loop).
- Commercial: provide high-level pilot economics (we can send a draft) and an optional short MSA/PO to accelerate the Dedicated reservation if you want guaranteed capacity.

Proposed benchmark windows: Sept 14–15 (US PDT), alternate Sept 21–22.  Please confirm which works for your team and whether the SLO targets above match your acceptance criteria.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Cheers,
Priyom

Hi Priyom — thanks for the clear summary and for capturing the MAP items.  A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Streaming expectations — we need the first partial token to arrive within ~120 ms on average for our in-product suggestions flow (web + Android). End-to-end completion for short prompts can tolerate up to ~450 ms because our client-side post-processing takes ~80–100 ms.  Can Redwood confirm how you measure token streaming latency (server-to-client vs. server-to-RT layer)?

2) Throughput / concurrency — 200 QPS sustained is within scope, but we have spikes during business hours that temporarily double QPS; how do you handle burst capacity and throttle behavior without violating the SLO?  Will we need reserved nodes?

3) Test data — attached is a small sample of 250 representative prompts (linked in Drive).  We will also include Mike as our infra lead for the benchmark window.

Finally, on the commercial side we would like a one-page pilot MSA or statement of work before the dedicated run so our procurement can green-light internal resources.  Could you route a short DocuSign for a pilot statement?

Regards,
Sarah

Looping in a few technical specifics from the infra side to set expectations for the benchmark and what configuration we recommend to meet the SLOs: 

- Measurement: Redwood measures streaming latency as the time from request arrival at the frontend load balancer to first byte delivered on the SSE/websocket channel (network + runtime). We can instrument client-side synthetic probes during the run so Bluehaven can see the server-to-client delta versus client-processing time.

- Meeting the 95p <= 300 ms target: achievable under the following recommended configuration for the pilot:
  * Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to avoid noisy neighbor effects during benchmark windows
  * KV prefix caching enabled for repeat prefixes; reduces P95 by ~20–30% for assistant-style workloads
  * Batch sizing tuned to average payload to avoid tail latency; we'll default to small continuous batches for streaming flows (batch timeout 6 ms).

- Throughput numbers (estimates): on our benchmark hardware (8xA100 equiv cluster):
  * Mixed short-turn workload (20–80 gen tokens): ~200–240 QPS sustained with P95 ~220–320 ms depending on model variant (float16 vs int8).
  * If Bluehaven needs 400 QPS peak for short windows, we recommend burst capacity (auto-burst to spare pool) or an elastic Dedicated ring — we can size this in the perf run.

- Concurrency (32 active sessions): we recommend reserving ~2–3 GPUs per 100 sustained QPS to maintain headroom; exact ratio will be validated in perf run.

Attached: perf_test_plan.xlsx (detailed test scenarios, dataset mix, measurement hooks).  We'll prepare a reproducible runbook and provide raw logs + P95/P99 histograms after the test.

If you want, we can run a short smoke test (5–10 minutes) ahead of the full window to validate connectivity and client handshake semantics.

—Ben
